answer: Topological Embedding Cost. Each new agent must be placed adjacent to existing agents that already route traffic through it; placement is accepted only if the newcomer occupies a distinct position in the relay graph rather than clustering near one hub. A raven node observed forwarding along a single corridor gets flagged as low-diversity. Sable agents must sustain inbound paths from at least three disjoint regions before receiving routing weight. The inlet from any fresh identity to the trusted core is capped by path-disjointness, so mass registration collapses into one thin channel.
